contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: Came at 1-1 in extra time of a final decided on penalties; a penalty would have given Birmingham a direct chance to take the lead.

contested_decisions.description: Sami Hyypiä, already booked (13'), brought down Joe Cole around half-time; Steve Bennett appeared to reach for his pocket, consulted his assistant and gave only a free-kick, so Hyypiä escaped a second yellow. CNN: Bennett 'looked set to issue another yellow card before realising what this would entail. Hyypia instead escaped'. ESPN timed it 45'; CNN 'just after the break'.
contested_decisions.assessed_by: no expert assessment found; journalist comments only (CNN/Reuters-style report; ESPN Soccernet live commentary)
contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: At 1-0 to Liverpool; a second yellow would have left Liverpool with 10 men for 75+ minutes including extra time. Chelsea nevertheless won, so it did not change the outcome against them; it could only have made Chelsea's win more likely.

contested_decisions.description: Steven Gerrard went down in the Chelsea area under a heavy challenge from Claude Makelele; no penalty. ESPN commentary: 'It could very easily have been given a penalty; the Frenchman was all over Gerrard.'
contested_decisions.assessed_by: no expert assessment found; journalist comments only (ESPN Soccernet live commentator)
contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: At 1-0 in a match Liverpool lost by one goal after extra time; a penalty could have produced a 2-0 lead.

contested_decisions.description: Chelsea manager José Mourinho, after putting his finger to his lips towards Liverpool fans when Chelsea equalised, was removed from the touchline to the tunnel. Mourinho said he was sent off by a policeman (who told the fourth official), not the referee; Independent says fourth official Phil Crossley and Football League refereeing official Jim Ashworth took him down the tunnel; referee Bennett to include it in his report.
contested_decisions.assessed_by: no expert assessment found; manager comments and journalists only
contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: Did not affect the players on the pitch; Chelsea won anyway. Recorded because it was disputed by Mourinho and executed by match officials, though initiated on police advice rather than as a refereeing decision.
